title: Database change
planning: Define data invariants, ownership, uniqueness, deletion behavior, and query access patterns before changing the schema.
Use database constraints for invariants that must survive concurrent requests; application checks alone are insufficient.
Plan a forward migration for existing rows and state whether rollback, backfill, or staged deployment is required.
Centralize the database client and domain queries instead of duplicating ORM access across route handlers.
checks: Apply migrations against both an empty database and representative existing data, then run affected route or service tests.
Test uniqueness, foreign-key, cascade or restrict behavior, transaction rollback, and concurrent writes.
Inspect generated SQL and query shape for missing indexes, over-fetching, and accidental full-table work.
review: Reject schema comments that stand in for migration design, required fields without backfills, and account deletion paths that ignore related rows.
Confirm money, timestamps, enums, and optionality use domain-appropriate database types.
